text:
chloe_sre: heads up — paging adapter (mux-connector) started suppressing pages around 09:12 UTC, several on-call pages never delivered. seeing lots of `suppress=true` in the logs.
ben_ops: on it. do we have a quick metric link?
chloe_sre: https://grafana.company/internal/d/abcd/pager-mux?orgId=1 — error rate/429s spiking, throttle key count exploded.
sam_oncall: I didn't get any pages at 09:13 — I was active and reachable. can someone confirm we didn't send to my phone?
emily_support: two customers opened critical tickets at 09:20 complaining they weren't paged by our notify flow. customer-impact flagging.
devops-bot: [ALERT] notify-mux-45: suppressor engaged (rate_limit). recent deploy: infra/pager-mux@v2.3.1 ~ 3h ago.
jorge_platform: that deploy included a splay change to the connector keying. possible dedupe key regression?
ben_ops: grabbing logs from the pod — `kubectl logs pager-mux-45 -n infra --since=20m | grep suppress`
ben_ops: log snippet: ```
2026-03-20T09:12:11Z WARN suppressor: key_count=1200 threshold=100 rate=500/s suppress=true
2026-03-20T09:12:12Z WARN dedupe: computed_key=host: ; hashed_key=0x0
2026-03-20T09:12:12Z ERROR delivery: downstream 429
```
chloe_sre: looks like empty header serialization -> many requests deduped to same key. that would overflow the suppressor.
sam_oncall: temporary mitigation: can someone manually page the affected customers / trigger SMS fallback? i'm standing by to confirm.
emily_support: manual SMS sent to the two customers and acknowledged. i've added a note to their tickets.
ben_ops: rolling a restart of the mux pod to flush current in-memory suppressor: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/pager-mux -n infra`
ben_ops: done — restarted all pods in the deployment. monitoring for delivery now.
devops-bot: [INFO] pager-mux pods restarted at 09:26 UTC — healthchecks passed.
chloe_sre: after restart delivery resumed for manual pages; incidentbot shows normal fanout. can we keep the restart as a short-term mitigation and roll back the splay change?
jorge_platform: yes — reverting the splay key change in the config and will cut a patch that validates header serialization before release. prioritizing a hotfix to incidentbot/dedupe logic.
ben_ops: creating rollback PR and a canary patch. also increasing suppressor threshold temporarily while we validate.
emily_support: customer impact recorded: 2 customers affected, ~14 minutes of missed pages (09:12-09:26). ops slack update sent to customers.
sam_oncall: all good on my end now. got a test page at 09:27.
chloe_sre: postmortem action items: 1) revert splay change (jorge) 2) add unit test for header serialization (eng) 3) add alert when suppressor key_count spikes (observability) 4) playbook blurb: manual paging fallback steps (docs).
incidentbot: created incident ticket INC-2026-03120-1 and attached logs.
ben_ops: will follow up with a short retro after the rollback. thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:
chloe_sre: closing thread — monitoring for 1hr, will escalate if regressions.
